This altricial neonate, born after a gestation that requires careful thermoregulation, is completely dependent on maternal care during the earliest phase of life. This relatively short intrauterine development, typical of many small-bodied subterranean rodents, results in offspring that are poorly developed at parturition. The neonatal period is characterized by rapid but concealed growth within the nesting burrow, where the mother provides both warmth and nutrition. Post-natal care is intensive, and the female must balance the energetic demands of lactation with the need to maintain her own body condition within the stable thermal environment of the underground burrow system.

Reaching this developmental milestone marks the transition from a non-reproductive sub-adult to a potentially breeding member of the population.
